Renewed
ree-NUDE
v. (past part.)
From Latin re (again) and novus (new), through the English renew. Webster 1828: made new again; repaired; restored to a former state or to a good state after decay; regenerated. Scripture uses it of strength restored, of the inward man daily repaired, and of the mind remade after the image of the Creator.

Biblical Definition

Renewed in the New Testament describes a daily work of God on the inward man that runs exactly opposite to what is happening to the body. For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16). Two processes, one man, opposite directions: the outward wasting, the inward repaired — and the wasting is the very cause Paul gives for not fainting. The renewal has a definite object and a definite pattern: And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him (Colossians 3:10). Knowledge is the sphere, and the pattern is the Creator’s own image, so that sanctification is the restoration of what Adam lost. Ephesians locates the work precisely: And be renewed in the spirit of your mind (Ephesians 4:23) — not the mind considered as intellect only but the governing disposition behind the thinking, which is why Romans 12:2 makes the renewing of the mind the means of proving the will of God. The Old Testament adds the promise to the waiting: they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles (Isaiah 40:31), and the psalmist marvels that God satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s (Psalm 103:5).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines RENEWED as made new; restored to a former or to a better state; repaired; refreshed; and, in theology, regenerated — renewed in the spirit of the mind by the operation of the Holy Spirit.

expand to see more

RENEWED, pp. — Made new again; restored to a former good state after decay, injury, or depravation.

Repeated; begun again; as, a renewed assault or a renewed covenant.

Refreshed; recruited; as, strength renewed by rest or by waiting upon God.

In theology, regenerated; renovated in heart and mind by the Holy Spirit after the image of God.

From Latin re, again, and novus, new — the root also of novel, innovate, and renovation.

Key Scripture

2 Corinthians 4:16 — "For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day."

Colossians 3:10 — "And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:"

Ephesians 4:23 — "And be renewed in the spirit of your mind;"

Isaiah 40:31 — "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."

Psalm 103:5 — "Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's."

Modern Corruption

The self-care industry has taken the vocabulary of renewal and detached it from God, so that the renewing of the mind is offered as a technique for restoring the self rather than the Spirit’s restoration of the Creator’s image in a fallen man.

expand to see more

Isaiah 40:31 is quoted more often on gym walls and coffee mugs than in any other setting, and almost always with its subject removed. The renewing belongs to them that wait upon the LORD; the promise is not that exhausted people recover if they rest but that people who look to God are carried by God. Detached from that clause the verse becomes a motivational slogan, and the slogan fails the first person whose strength does not return — which is precisely the situation Isaiah was addressing, a nation in exile with nothing left. The chapter opens with Comfort ye, comfort ye my people and grounds the comfort in the everlasting God who fainteth not, neither is weary. The strength renewed is His, lent, not the sufferer’s own reserve rediscovered.

The second displacement is therapeutic. Romans 12:2 and Ephesians 4:23 are routinely enlisted for programmes of thought-management in which the renewed mind means an inventory of negative self-talk replaced with affirmations. Colossians 3:10 gives the actual content and pattern: renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him. The knowledge is knowledge of God, the pattern is the imago Dei defaced in Adam, and the agent is the Spirit through the Word. Where the technique is aimed at a better opinion of the self, Scripture aims at a truer knowledge of God and a lower estimate of the self, and 2 Corinthians 4:16 is content to let the outward man perish while that work goes on.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek anakainoo (G341), to renew, to make new in quality; anakainosis (G342), renewal; ananeoo (G365), to renew in the spirit of the mind; Hebrew chadash (H2318), to be new, to renew, to repair.

expand to see more

Greek anakainoo (G341) — to make new in quality, not merely new in time; 2 Corinthians 4:16 and Colossians 3:10.

Greek anakainosis (G342) — renewal; the renewing of the Holy Ghost (Titus 3:5) and the renewing of your mind (Romans 12:2).

Greek ananeoo (G365) — to renew, to make young again; only at Ephesians 4:23, of the spirit of the mind.

Hebrew chadash (H2318) — to renew, repair, rebuild; used of repairing the altar and of renewing the kingdom (2 Chronicles 15:8; 1 Samuel 11:14).

Hebrew chalaph (H2498) — to change, to pass on, to renew; behind shall renew their strength in Isaiah 40:31.

Usage

"The inward man is renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16) — two opposite processes in one man."

"Renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him (Colossians 3:10) — sanctification as restored image."

"They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength (Isaiah 40:31) — the promise with its subject kept in place."
